chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'la, from Is'haq, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding a man who merges a thirty-dirham piece of cloth with another man's twenty-dirham piece of cloth, so the two parcels were sent, and it was not recognized whether this was his cloth or that was his cloth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The two pieces of cloth are sold, and the owner of the thirty is given three-fifths of the price, and the other is given two-fifths of the price.' I said: 'So if the owner of the twenty said to the owner of the thirty, "Choose whichever of the two you desire,"' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He has been fair.'
ai.seo_question: How is profit divided when mixed goods of different values become indistinguishable?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi addresses the fiqh of *khalṭ* (commingling) where goods of distinct values become indistinguishable, establishing a default proportional division of proceeds based on original capital contribution. The narration highlights the Shia juristic principle of *iḥtiyāṭ* (precaution) versus *iḥsān* (equity), noting that while the strict legal share is three-fifths to the higher-value owner, allowing the lower-value owner to choose the item is deemed a fair and acceptable alternative, reflecting the importance of mutual consent in commercial transactions.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Musa Bin Sa’dan, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’la, from Is’haq,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding the man who merged a thirty Dirham piece of cloth, with another man with twenty Dirhams piece of cloth. So the two parcels were sent, and it was not recognised whether this was his cloth, or this was not his cloth. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So the two pieces of cloth would be sold, so the owner of the thirty would be given three-fifths of the price, and the other one would be given two-fifths of the price’. I said, ‘So if the owner of the twenty said to the owner of the thirty, ‘Choose whichever of the two you so desire to?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He has been fair’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn Sa‘dan from al-Husayn ibn abu aI-‘Ala’ from Ishaq who has narrated the following: “This is about the case of a man to whom one man sends thirty dirham in a piece of cloth, another man sends him twenty dirham in a piece of cloth and they become mixed so much that he cannot distinguish. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He must give three-fifths of the value to the man of thirty dirham and two-fifths of the value to the other one.’
I then said the man with thirty has said to the man with twenty, take whichever you like. He (the Imam) said, ‘He has been fair.’”
